decisions.reason: This module fits tightly with the firm's apron systems and integration knowledge, so accumulated deployment learning and existing R&D make continued improvement and retention likely.

Billing is less central than operational control, but it still draws on the firm's airport data, software, and platform integration capabilities, so management would likely keep it while refining its role in the broader offering.
Apron equipment monitoring builds directly on the firm's installed-base experience, maintenance know-how, and digital service direction, which supports further learning and lowers exit risk.

Resource management remains close to the firm's core airport efficiency expertise, and service feedback from projects gives it the absorptive capacity to keep improving and commercialising the product.

The safety alert service matches the firm's safety-critical systems knowledge and benefits from in-house R&D and a market moving toward automated operations, so management would continue backing it despite careful monitoring of adoption.
